text:
TCK-001 (requirement): Sellers can set a reserve price

When listing an item a seller can set an optional reserve price, at least the starting price. If the auction closes with a highest bid below the reserve, the item is unsold and no winner is announced. Bidders see whether the reserve is met, never its amount.

I saved the plan for TCK-001. It starts at **P1 (requirements)** because the ticket adds a new rule and changes two existing ones. The plan has no open questions.

**Requirements (P1)**
- A new requirement, "Reserve price":
  - A seller can set an optional reserve when listing an item. A reserve below the starting price is rejected.
  - If the highest bid at close is below the reserve, the item is unsold and has no winner.
  - Bidders only see whether the reserve is met, never the amount.
- REQ-001 (listing an item) will mention the optional reserve.
- REQ-004 (closing an auction) currently always makes the highest bidder the winner. It will be changed so that a reserve that isn't met gives an unsold item with no winner.

**Design and code that change**
- **Item and item view (DSN-015, DSN-017):** the item stores a reserve price. Clients get only a "reserve met" flag.
- **Listing an item (DSN-019, DSN-022, UC-002, SEQ-002):** takes and checks the optional reserve.
- **Closing an auction (UC-005, SEQ-005):** closing checks the reserve before naming a winner.
- **Item store (DSN-029):** saves the reserve as a new database column.
- **Live events (DSN-030, DSN-031, UC-003):** the bid and close events carry "reserve met" but not the amount.
- **Web page (DSN-042):** the listing form gets a reserve field, and the item page shows whether the reserve is met.

**Why the routes are in the plan:** today `app.ts` returns the whole stored item from `GET /api/items` and `GET /api/items/:id`. Once the item holds a reserve, those routes would show its amount to bidders, so the plan has them leave it out.

**Tests:** new tests in the UC-002, UC-003, UC-005 and DSN-029 test files. They cover the reserve check, closing below and above the reserve, that no response or event exposes the amount, and that the store saves and reads the reserve back.

The code currently matches the design (no drift), so nothing else needs fixing first.
Close TCK-001 and write the change report.

I saved the change report and closed TCK-001. The final test run had 57 passed and 0 failed.

**What changed in each phase:**
- **Requirements:** REQ-012 is new and covers the reserve price. REQ-001 now lists the reserve as an optional field. REQ-004 has the new close rules: the highest bidder wins only if there is no reserve or the reserve is met, otherwise the item is unsold. Changing or removing a reserve after listing was added to out of scope.
- **Design:** Item now has a reserve price and two new methods, one that says whether the reserve is met and one that closes the auction. A new PublicItem (DSN-044) is what gets sent to clients: it shows whether the reserve is met and never the amount. The item controller, item service and item view now return it.
- **Code:** listings with a reserve below the starting price are rejected. The reserve is saved to the database, and older databases get the new column when the server starts. Live bid and close events now say whether the reserve is met. The web page has an optional reserve field and shows "reserve met" or "reserve not met".
- **Tests:** six test files were updated to the new signatures, and new tests cover the reserve rules.

**Still open:**
- **Three assumptions in the requirements need confirming:**
  - the reserve is in the item's currency
  - whether sellers can see their own reserve amount (right now nobody can after listing)
  - items without a reserve show no reserve label at all
- **"No admin role" in REQ-008 has no design element.** Someone needs to decide whether the design as a whole counts as covering it.
- **The live event's contents aren't in the design.** The UC-004 test expects a `reserveMet` field in bid events; the code sends it, but the design doesn't say it should.
- **Two things to check by hand:** the renumbered REQ-004 tests (AC2 to AC6) and the updated scenario tests for listing, closing and viewing prices (SEQ-002, SEQ-005, SEQ-006) should still match the requirements. No test covers the reserve display on the web page.
